breakfast.name: Ugali na Dagaa (Cornmeal with Sardines)
instructions: Make thick ugali from cornmeal
Fry dagaa with tomatoes and onion
Serve together
breakfast.description: Cornmeal porridge with fried sardines — Lake Victoria staple.

breakfast.name: Vitumbua (Rice Cakes)
instructions: Mix batter, rise 30 min
Pour into half-sphere pan
Cook until golden
breakfast.description: Sweet coconut rice cakes from Zanzibar.

breakfast.name: Maandazi (East African Doughnuts)
instructions: Maandazi are the East African fried dough -- eaten from Kenya to Tanzania to Mozambique
Slightly sweet, cardamom-scented dough deep-fried
Triangle or oval shape
The coconut milk and cardamom are the East African flavor profile
Eaten for breakfast with tea
Sold at street stalls from the early morning
breakfast.description: East African fried dough -- maandazi, slightly sweet cardamom-scented dough deep-fried into triangles or ovals. Coconut milk and cardamom are the East African flavor profile. Eaten for breakfast with tea across Kenya, Tanzania, and Mozambique.

breakfast.name: Uji (Porridge)
ingredients: Fermented millet or sorghum flour (uji flour)
instructions: Uji is the East African fermented grain porridge
Made from fermented millet or sorghum -- slightly sour from fermentation
Drunk more than eaten -- liquid enough to drink from a cup
Sweetened with sugar or eaten savory
A traditional baby food and everyday breakfast across East Africa
breakfast.description: East African fermented grain porridge -- uji, fermented millet or sorghum thinned to a drinkable consistency. Slightly sour from fermentation. Sweetened with sugar or eaten savory. Traditional baby food and everyday breakfast across East Africa.

lunch.name: Pilau ya Wali (Zanzibari Pilau)
ingredients: Pilau spices: cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, cumin, black pepper
instructions: Fry onion until very dark
Add meat and spices
Add rice and water
Cook covered
Serve topped with caramelized onion
lunch.description: Zanzibari spiced rice — aromatic and golden.

lunch.name: Nyama Choma (Grilled Meat)
instructions: Season meat with lime and salt
Grill over charcoal until done
Slice against grain
Serve with ugali and chili sauce

lunch.name: Biriyani (Tanzanian Style)
ingredients: Biriyani spice mix: cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, cumin, coriander, turmeric
Saffron or food coloring (for the yellow-orange color)
instructions: Tanzanian biriyani is a legacy of the Arab and Indian coastal trade
Zanzibar island was a major Arab trading post -- the Swahili Coast spice trade
The Omani Arabs controlled Zanzibar from the 17th to 19th centuries
Indian traders brought biriyani from the subcontinent
The Tanzanian version: rich with cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon
Eaten at celebrations, weddings, and Eid
Zanzibar biriyani is particularly famous
lunch.description: Tanzanian Zanzibar-style biriyani -- basmati rice layered with marinated chicken or goat, fragrant with cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, and coriander, garnished with fried onion and raisins. Legacy of the Arab and Indian Swahili Coast trade: Oman controlled Zanzibar from the 17th-19th centuries. Eaten at celebrations and Eid.

lunch.name: Mishkaki (Grilled Skewers)
ingredients: Marinade: garlic, ginger, lemon, coconut milk, chilli, cumin, coriander, turmeric
instructions: Mishkaki are the Tanzanian grilled meat skewers
The marinade has coconut milk and lemon -- the East African coastal flavor
Grilled over charcoal
Sold at street stalls in the evening
The coconut and lime marinade gives a distinctly coastal Swahili character
lunch.description: Tanzanian grilled meat skewers -- beef or chicken marinated in garlic, ginger, coconut milk, lemon, and East African spices, grilled over charcoal. The coconut-lime marinade is the Swahili coastal signature. Sold at street stalls in the evening.

lunch.name: Wali wa Nazi (Coconut Rice)
instructions: Wali wa nazi is the Tanzanian coconut rice -- the staple of the Swahili Coast
Rice cooked in coconut milk -- the coconut milk replaces water
The rice absorbs all the coconut milk
Fragrant and slightly sweet
Eaten with every coastal Tanzanian meal: with fish, stews, or kachumbari
lunch.description: Tanzanian coconut rice -- jasmine rice cooked in coconut milk (replacing water entirely), fragrant and slightly sweet. The staple of the Swahili Coast. Eaten with fish, stews, and kachumbari (tomato-onion salad).

dinner.name: Mchuzi wa Samaki (Fish Curry)
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, curry
Add tomatoes and coconut milk
Add fish, simmer 15 min
Add tamarind and lime
dinner.description: Coastal fish curry in coconut milk.

dinner.name: Ndizi na Nyama (Plantains with Meat)
instructions: Brown meat
Add onion, tomatoes, curry
Add plantains and coconut milk
Simmer until tender
dinner.description: Meat and plantain stew in coconut milk.

dinner.name: Samaki wa Kupaka (Grilled Fish in Coconut Sauce)
instructions: Samaki wa kupaka is the Zanzibar and coastal Tanzania grilled fish dish
The fish is marinated, grilled, then basted with a coconut-tomato sauce
The sauce: coconut milk cooked with spices and tomato until thick
The kupaka means to apply/paint in Swahili -- the sauce is applied to the fish
Eaten at Zanzibar waterfront restaurants and street stalls
dinner.description: Zanzibar grilled fish with coconut sauce -- whole fish grilled, then basted with a coconut milk-tomato-spice sauce (kupaka: to apply/paint in Swahili). The sauce thickens over the fish on the grill. Eaten at Zanzibar waterfront stalls.

dinner.name: Mchuzi wa Kuku (Chicken Curry)
ingredients: Curry powder (East African blend), turmeric, cumin
instructions: Mchuzi wa kuku is the Tanzanian chicken curry
Mchuzi = sauce/curry in Swahili; kuku = chicken
A tomato-onion base cooked with curry spices and coconut milk
The Indian curry influence through the Swahili Coast Indian community
Served with wali (rice) or ugali (cornmeal)
dinner.description: Tanzanian chicken curry -- chicken braised in a tomato-onion sauce with East African curry spices and coconut milk. Mchuzi (sauce) wa kuku (chicken): the Swahili name. The Indian curry influence via the Swahili Coast Indian community. Served with rice or ugali.

dinner.name: Pilau (Tanzanian Spiced Rice)
ingredients: Pilau masala: cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, cumin, black pepper
instructions: Tanzanian pilau is different from Indian pilaf and Iranian pilau
The spice blend (pilau masala) is the Swahili Coast version
The rice is first fried with onion and the pilau masala
Then broth from the cooked meat is added
The whole spices are eaten with the rice
Made for celebrations -- a festive rice dish
dinner.description: Tanzanian Swahili spiced rice -- pilau masala (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, cumin) fried with rice and onion, then meat broth added. The Swahili Coast spice tradition differs from Indian and Iranian pilaf. Made for celebrations and special occasions.

snacks.name: Mishkaki (Meat Skewers)
instructions: Marinate beef
Thread on skewers
Grill over charcoal
snacks.description: Charcoal-grilled beef skewers — Dar es Salaam street food.

snacks.name: Vitumbua (Coconut Rice Cakes)
instructions: Vitumbua are the Tanzanian and Kenyan fermented coconut rice cakes
A rice flour batter with coconut milk and cardamom
Cooked in a special pan with round indentations (like a Danish aebleskiver pan)
Small, round, and slightly crispy outside
Soft inside from the fermentation
Sold at Tanzanian coastal markets
snacks.description: Tanzanian coconut rice cakes -- fermented rice flour and coconut milk batter with cardamom, cooked in a round-indentation pan until crispy outside and soft inside. The Swahili Coast snack sold at coastal markets.

snacks.name: Zanzibar Pizza (Urojo Mix)
ingredients: Thin dough (stretched thin on the griddle)
instructions: Zanzibar pizza is a Zanzibar street food specialty -- not a pizza at all
A thin dough stretched on a griddle
Filled with spiced meat, vegetables, and a cracked egg
Folded and cooked until the egg is set
Eaten at the Forodhani Gardens night market in Stone Town, Zanzibar
A Zanzibari invention that has no connection to Italian pizza
snacks.description: Zanzibar street food pancake -- thin dough stretched on a griddle, filled with spiced meat, onion, tomato, and egg, folded and cooked. Called Zanzibar pizza but unrelated to Italian pizza. The specialty of Forodhani Gardens night market in Stone Town.

snacks.name: Kachumbari (Fresh Tomato-Onion Salad)
instructions: Kachumbari is the East African fresh salad -- eaten across Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda
Fresh tomatoes and raw onion dressed with lemon juice
The simplest and most ubiquitous East African condiment-salad
Eaten alongside grilled meat, rice, or ugali
snacks.description: East African fresh tomato-onion salad -- kachumbari, diced ripe tomatoes with thinly sliced red onion, coriander, and lemon juice. The ubiquitous East African condiment eaten alongside grilled meat, rice, and ugali across Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.

desserts.name: Kashata (Coconut Brittle)
instructions: Cook sugar until caramelized
Add coconut and cardamom
Pour onto tray
Let harden, break into pieces

desserts.name: Zanzibar Halua (Spiced Halva)
instructions: Zanzibar halua is the Zanzibari halva -- very different from Middle Eastern sesame halva
Made from corn starch or wheat starch cooked with coconut milk and sugar
Heavily spiced with cardamom and rosewater
Saffron gives a golden color
Soft and gelatinous -- not crumbly like sesame halva
Sold in Zanzibar's spice markets
desserts.description: Zanzibar corn starch halva -- cooked corn starch and coconut milk with sugar, cardamom, rosewater, and saffron into a soft, gelatinous confection. Different from sesame halva: soft and sticky. Sold in Zanzibar's spice markets.

desserts.name: Andazi (Sweet Flatbread)
ingredients: Flour, coconut milk, sugar, cardamom, yeast
instructions: Andazi is the Tanzanian sweet flatbread -- slightly different from maandazi
Thinner and more like a sweet flatbread than a doughnut
Coconut milk and cardamom flavor
Eaten as a snack or dessert
desserts.description: Tanzanian sweet flatbread -- andazi, thin coconut-cardamom flavored bread eaten as a snack or dessert. Slightly different from maandazi (doughnut): flatter and less fried.

drinks.name: Tangawizi (Ginger Drink)
instructions: Grate ginger, squeeze juice
Mix with lemon, sugar, water
Chill

drinks.name: Konyagi
instructions: Serve with tonic or cola
Tanzania's national spirit

drinks.name: Tangawizi (Ginger Tea)
instructions: Tangawizi means ginger in Swahili
A strongly spiced ginger tea -- very gingery
Made by simmering fresh ginger in water, then adding tea and sugar
Popular across East Africa -- warming and medicinal
The Swahili Coast spice trade made ginger easily available
drinks.description: Tanzanian ginger tea -- tangawizi (ginger in Swahili), fresh ginger simmered in water, black tea and sugar added. Very gingery and warming. Popular across East Africa as both a beverage and a remedy. The Swahili Coast spice trade made ginger an everyday ingredient.
